short: Maastricht, Black Wednesday, and the first steps of the Irish peace process.
full:
John Major, who had left school at sixteen, succeeded Thatcher in November 1990 and unexpectedly won the 1992 election with over fourteen million votes, more than any party has taken before or since. He negotiated British opt-outs from the single currency and the social chapter at Maastricht, then spent years fighting his own Eurosceptic backbenchers to ratify the treaty.

On 16 September 1992 speculators drove sterling out of the European exchange rate mechanism; interest rates were raised twice in one day and then abandoned, and the Conservative reputation for economic competence never recovered, even as growth resumed and inflation stayed low. He privatised the railways, launched the National Lottery, and with Albert Reynolds issued the Downing Street Declaration of 1993, which led to IRA and loyalist ceasefires the following year. Labour's landslide in May 1997 ended eighteen years of Conservative government.
